title: The wind that cancels your port day
subtitle: It has a name, a season and a time of day — and a good itinerary is built around all three.

text: A ship anchored in sight of an island is still a missed port.
sub: If the tenders cannot run, the day is gone. Nobody sells you that risk when you book the sailing in August.

title: Three things it decides for you

items.head: It peaks in July and August
items.body: A dry northerly funnelling down the Aegean, at its most insistent in the height of summer.

items.head: It builds through the afternoon
items.body: Mornings are usually the calm half of the day. This is why I want you ashore early, not after lunch.

items.head: It rewrites the itinerary
items.body: Wind or swell can suspend tendering outright, and an exposed anchorage gets swapped at short notice.

right.label: At anchor
items: A hard day on stiff knees

points.label: May - June
points.value: Generally settled. The wind is present but not yet the organising fact of the day.

points.label: July - August
points.value: Meltemi season proper, strongest in the afternoons. Plan mornings ashore.

points.label: September
points.value: The wind eases and the sea is at its warmest. The month I argue for.

points.label: Mid-October on
points.value: First autumn systems arrive. Fewer crowds, more need for flexibility.

text: You cannot book the weather. You can book the exposure.
sub: Ask which calls are tender ports, which are alongside, and where the wind sits in that week. Then choose the itinerary that fails gracefully.

title: Save this before you book an August sailing
body: Or send me the itinerary and I'll mark the calls that depend on a calm afternoon — and what I'd sail instead.
